name: Conrad Mann
life: “I still remember the first month my chair rent came before groceries.” On Sunday, near Paper & Pine Books, Conrad starts with the handwritten shelf cards and often leaves with a suggestion for somebody else.
voice: I rent my chair and earn well. I never tell newcomers my partner pays our mortgage.
appearance: Conrad is easy to recognize by a center part and straight chestnut hair and a wide brow and a narrow jaw. Usually dressed in an olive canvas jacket with a square of clean cloth for polishing smudges, Conrad presses the lips together to keep a smile in when listening.
personality: Conrad has a talent for getting adversaries to laugh at exactly the same thing. Conrad knows better than to expect the laugh to settle what they are arguing about.
agenda: To tell new renters what outside income made the first year possible.
family: Lee Murphy is Conrad’s first cousin once removed. Conrad asks the question the rest of the family avoided. Lee chooses an ordinary story to tell. They tend to get further with an important subject when it arrives in the middle of talk about dinner or work. Asked about *A ship without postcards*, Lee says, “I found our old dance hall in the background of a harbor print and sent it to my ex.”
connections: Emil Lund. A renter whose home costs are covered shows the prospective owner what the chair alone really costs.

reactions.situation: A regular cancels the week's most valuable appointment
reactions.response: Conrad revises the week's numbers with the cancellation included before making any promise.
